screening_of_unoptimized_candidates.rule: declared dominance screen: lower reference activity AND higher metal price than current lowest-cost candidate

chosen_args.why_stop: Stopping rule is satisfied. A feasible lowest-cost candidate exists; all other candidates are either optimized or screened by the declared dominance rule; the highest-activity candidate differs from the industrial choice and has been assessed by BACKWARD plus TEST_REACHABILITY. Remaining affordable actions have low expected decision value: exact CHECK_MODEL_VALIDITY and MC are unaffordable, while additional small lever tests would not plausibly overturn the large cost gap and dominance-screen result.

main_risks: The full admissible process domain was not built because it was unaffordable; final evidence uses an economically focused window plus a local expanded window.
candidate_13 optimum lies at Tsep_C=30.0, the upper edge of the admissible separator-temperature domain; exact edge validity check was unaffordable with remaining budget.
Descriptor uncertainty MC was unaffordable, so probabilistic robustness was not quantified.
mitigations: Local expanded window improved candidate_13 and preserved ranking versus the only higher-activity contenders.
All unoptimized candidates satisfy the declared screen relative to candidate_13: lower reference activity and higher metal price.
Highest-activity candidate candidate_04 would need a 201.22x intrinsic-activity gain for parity, far above the maximum 2.52x gain available across process states on the frozen descriptor manifold.
